A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T2ISafety/ImageGuard work. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–H, including equations, figures and tables, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageGuard experiments, component ablations, human-evaluation agreement, and safety evaluations of generation models and concept-erasing methods.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds safety results for three generation models and two concept-erasing methods in Tables 4 and 5.

M1.justification: ImageGuard retains its InternLM-XComposer2 base, instruction templates, gated cross-modality attention, selected 24-block configuration, and combined contrastive and autoregressive loss. No proposed algorithm or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: The T2ISafety data sources, 12 tasks and 44 categories, and UnsafeDiff, SMID and UnsafeBench evaluations are retained. The added models perform the existing image-generation task without introducing new datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds LlamaGen, Show-o and Vila-u, extending the original diffusion-model comparison to autoregressive/unified models. Table 5 adds ESD and MACE alongside UCE and SLD. Together these substantially broaden the generation and defense comparison sets; ImageGuard's evaluator baselines in Table 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The 2,669 evaluation prompts, category counts, safety-rate/NKL and F1 metrics, data splits, and ImageGuard training settings are retained. The added comparisons use the existing benchmark; no revised evaluation procedure is reported.

E4.justification: Table 5 extends the existing analysis of concept erasing against malicious prompts to ESD and MACE across the same six toxicity classes. Component ablations, OOD evaluations, human agreement, prompt-distribution analysis and attention visualizations otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are added, and the appendix's human-agreement statistics are retained.

E6.justification: Additional comparator results change the leaders: Table 4 reports Show-o privacy safety of 0.742 versus the previous leader SDXL's retained 0.672. Table 5 adds ESD at 0.642 and MACE at 0.799 overall, exceeding the previous best only for MACE (UCE: 0.711). Existing result rows, including ImageGuard's results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The normalized KL definition, uniform-reference assumption, entropy bounds and Appendix F derivation are unchanged, as are the mathematical descriptions of attention and training losses.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the safety taxonomy and dataset, ImageGuard's evaluation advantages, normalized KL fairness measurement, and persistent safety problems in generation models.

C2.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 retain their safety interpretations and defense limitations. Appendix A's misinformation/deepfake limitation and Appendix H's mechanism explanations are unchanged; the added model results receive no substantive new interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 removes the explicit explanation that SLD shares SD-v1.5 weights and UCE uses it as the target, replacing it with generic default-setting language for four defenses. Appendix implementation details and the code/data release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Four references are added for MACE, LlamaGen, Vila-u and Show-o. All 78 earlier references are retained; ESD was already cited in v1. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 5.1 gains a short description of the added generation models and revises the defense setup paragraph. An affiliation and minor grammar are corrected. The main section sequence and appendix narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 4 and 5 gain rows within their existing formats, causing local reflow of the discussion, conclusion and references. All figures and appendix tables retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: The additional generation paradigms and defense methods make the benchmark's comparisons less dependent on the original model selection, providing a modest empirical benefit. Integration is incomplete: Section 5.2 still calls SDXL the privacy leader despite Show-o's higher Table 4 score, and Section 5.3 still discusses 'both' defenses after the comparison expands to four.
